timeline.text: How do huge companies keep permissions under control?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: They automate it. Manual review doesn't survive scale.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Yes. Analyze what each identity actually uses and revoke the rest.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Exactly. Netflix's tool removes permissions nobody used. Least privilege as a service.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: TTL-based access. Privileges expire automatically after a time-to-live.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Secret detection scans repositories. Keep credentials out of source.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Distributed firewalls and network policies. Segmentation that scales with the fleet.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Syscall auditing and endpoint monitoring across every host.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So the platform does the security work?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Yes. Bake it in, automate the boring parts, and measure so it stays correct.
